l4_steps.name: Validate Interline Ticketing Agreement status
l4_steps.input: Partner carrier IATA code, agreement reference number
l4_steps.output: ITA validity confirmation and billing currency code
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of active partners with valid ITA before ticket issuance enabled
l4_steps.pain_point: MITA agreements lapse without automated renewal alerts — expired ITAs cause ticket rejection at GDS, creating passenger disruption and manual escalation to partner airline's commercial team

l4_steps.name: Load partner carrier tariff and fare rules
l4_steps.input: Partner carrier tariff filing, IATA fare construction rules
l4_steps.output: Loaded fare table with combinability and routing rules
l4_steps.kpi: Tariff load completed within 24 hours of ATPCO effective date
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO batch updates publish at 00:01 EST — late-night automation failures leave stale fare rules in production until manual intervention, causing mispriced interline itineraries

l4_steps.name: Configure MITA SSR message formats in PSS
l4_steps.input: Partner carrier EDIFACT profile, SSR/OSI message templates
l4_steps.output: Configured interline messaging profiles in Altéa
l4_steps.pain_point: EDIFACT PADIS message version mismatches between carriers require manual mapping tables — each new partner requires 2–4 weeks of IT configuration, delaying commercial go-live

l4_steps.name: Register codeshare flight designator in Amadeus Altéa
l4_steps.input: Operating carrier flight schedule, codeshare agreement terms
l4_steps.output: Codeshare flight records in SSIM format, loaded to Altéa inventory
l4_steps.kpi: Codeshare schedule loaded ≥90 days before first departure date
l4_steps.pain_point: Operating carrier schedule changes propagate with latency — SkyWORKS SSIM refresh cycle is 24 hours, meaning same-day schedule swaps create ghost codeshare flights visible in GDS

l4_steps.name: Sync partner inventory blocks via EDIFACT SSR/ACK
l4_steps.input: Codeshare seat block allocation from operating carrier
l4_steps.output: Confirmed inventory allocation in Altéa booking classes
l4_steps.kpi: Inventory sync acknowledgement (ACK) received within 15 minutes of block request
l4_steps.pain_point: Dual inventory control (marketing vs operating carrier) creates overbooking risk — NRM cannot directly query operating carrier's live seat map, relying on asynchronous SSR messages with no guaranteed delivery SLA

l4_steps.name: File codeshare fares via ATPCO and validate combinability
l4_steps.input: Agreed codeshare fare levels, routing restrictions, booking class mapping
l4_steps.output: Published codeshare fare filing with combinability Cat 10/11 rules
l4_steps.kpi: Zero misfiled combinability rules causing GDS pricing errors at launch
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO Category 10 combinability rules are complex — errors in end-on-end fare construction go undetected until passengers receive incorrect fares at booking, requiring mass repricing and IROPS-level agent intervention

l4_steps.name: Receive interline booking request from GDS or NDC
l4_steps.input: Agent PNR with multi-carrier itinerary, passenger name, fare basis
l4_steps.output: Interline booking record with all carrier segments confirmed
l4_steps.kpi: GDS booking response time ≤3 seconds for interline itineraries
l4_steps.pain_point: NDC-sourced interline bookings lack standardised offer/order IDs compatible with legacy EDIFACT settlement — carriers without full NDC back-office integration cannot receive or settle NDC-issued interline tickets

l4_steps.name: Perform fare construction combinability check
l4_steps.input: Multi-carrier itinerary, fare basis codes, routing
l4_steps.output: Approved fare construction or rejected itinerary with reason code
l4_steps.kpi: Fare construction error rate ≤0.5% of all interline transactions
l4_steps.pain_point: Half-round-trip (HRT) and end-on-end combination logic in Altéa pricing engine has known edge cases for 3+ carrier itineraries — manual audit required for itineraries crossing IATA traffic conference areas

l4_steps.name: Issue interline e-ticket via BSP or ARC
l4_steps.input: Approved fare construction, PNR, passenger data, payment details
l4_steps.output: Interline e-ticket (ET) with all coupons, transmitted to BSP/ARC
l4_steps.kpi: Ticket issuance success rate ≥99.8%; time-to-issue ≤60 seconds
l4_steps.pain_point: BSP settlement reporting requires per-coupon carrier code validation — system-generated document check digit errors in Altéa have caused bulk ticket voids requiring 48-hour manual reissue queues

l4_steps.name: Transmit PNR and coupon data to operating carrier
l4_steps.input: Issued e-ticket coupons, booking class, SSR elements
l4_steps.output: EDIFACT PNRGOV / IATCI message delivered to partner carrier PSS
l4_steps.kpi: PNR transmission to operating carrier within 5 minutes of ticket issuance; delivery confirmation ≥99%
l4_steps.pain_point: IATCI (Interline Through Check-In) handoff failures occur when operating carrier's PSS is on a different version of the EDIFACT PADIS standard — passengers arrive at operating carrier's check-in counter with no booking record

l4_steps.name: Calculate revenue proration using IATA Proration rules
l4_steps.input: Issued ticket coupons, fare basis, mileage/unit proration method
l4_steps.output: Proration memo per carrier with amounts in billing currency
l4_steps.kpi: Proration calculation completed within T+1 business day of travel date
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA Proration Rules Manual (PRM) updates twice yearly — revenue accounting system requires manual rule table updates, and delayed updates cause incorrect proration splits that take months to detect via interline billing reconciliation

l4_steps.name: Generate and submit interline billing memo via IATA CASS
l4_steps.system: IATA CASS (Cargo Accounts Settlement System) / ICH
l4_steps.input: Proration memos, coupon usage data, billing period cutoff
l4_steps.output: Interline billing memo (IBM) submitted to IATA Clearing House
l4_steps.kpi: Billing memo submission before monthly IATA ICH cutoff (25th of month); dispute rate ≤2%
l4_steps.pain_point: ICH submission deadlines are fixed — revenue accounting system outages during the last 3 business days of the month result in missed cutoffs, deferring settlement by a full month and creating cash flow exposure

l4_steps.name: Reconcile and approve interline billing statements
l4_steps.input: Partner carrier billing memos, internal proration calculations
l4_steps.output: Reconciled statement with approved, disputed, and pending items
l4_steps.kpi: Reconciliation completed within 10 business days of billing statement receipt; dispute resolution ≤30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Coupon usage data gaps (e.g., missing lift coupons from operating carrier) prevent automated matching — manual reconciliation for unmatched coupons exceeds 200 hours/month at mid-size carriers

l4_steps.name: Post approved proration revenue to general ledger
l4_steps.input: Approved interline billing statement, GL account mapping
l4_steps.output: Revenue journal entries posted to SAP GL with interline partner cost centre
l4_steps.kpi: GL posting completed within 2 business days of billing approval; zero unposted items at month-end close
l4_steps.pain_point: Interline revenue accounting system integration with SAP FI relies on nightly batch file transfer — intra-month adjustments require manual journal entries, increasing month-end close effort and audit trail risk

l4_steps.name: Detect schedule disruption affecting interline itinerary
l4_steps.input: IROPS alert from operating carrier, flight cancellation or delay >3 hours
l4_steps.output: Affected interline PNR list flagged for rebooking action
l4_steps.kpi: Disruption notification to marketing carrier within 30 minutes of operating carrier declaring IROPS
l4_steps.pain_point: Operating carrier IROPS notifications arrive via unstructured email or telephone — no automated EDIFACT OC (Other Communication) message standard exists, meaning marketing carrier agents learn of disruptions reactively when passengers call

l4_steps.name: Reroute passenger on alternate interline or codeshare flight
l4_steps.input: Disrupted PNR, alternate routing options, IATA Resolution 735d rebooking rules
l4_steps.output: Reprotected PNR on new itinerary, updated coupons transmitted to operating carrier
l4_steps.kpi: Passenger reprotection offer presented within 60 minutes of IROPS declaration; acceptance rate ≥85%
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA Resolution 735d mandates specific rebooking rules for involuntary rerouting — agents are not always trained on which rules apply to each interline agreement, leading to incorrect fare differences being charged or waived

l4_steps.name: Process interline ticket reissue or refund
l4_steps.input: Original e-ticket coupons, rerouting decision, applicable waiver code
l4_steps.output: Reissued ticket or refund application submitted to BSP with ADM/ACM if required
l4_steps.kpi: Reissue or refund processing completed within 24 hours of passenger request; ADM dispute rate ≤1%
l4_steps.pain_point: BSP Agent Debit Memos (ADMs) for incorrectly waived change fees create disputes lasting 6–12 months — interline reissue waiver codes are not standardised across carriers, causing downstream billing errors that inflate interline dispute volumes
